title: Cambridge truck ban and basic income advocacy
subtitle: Also: Conestoga U-Pass support, CUPE settlement, Breslau library, new strategic plan, blue box transition, airport café.
overview: Regional Council voted to divert heavy trucks from downtown Cambridge onto the new McQueen Shaver Boulevard, with a ban on several downtown streets including Concession Street. Staff were also directed to build noise walls along about 1.5 km of McQueen Shaver and to improve active transportation on Concession. Council asked for a compliance update in summer 2024. This responds to long-standing resident concerns about truck traffic in residential areas.

Council asked the province to raise Ontario Works and ODSP rates and tie them to inflation. It also backed a guaranteed liveable basic income and directed the Regional Chair to write to federal and provincial leaders {{vote:m22}}. Council supported in principle a Conestoga College U-Pass as early as September 2024, subject to budget approval and a student referendum. It also approved a tentative CUPE Local 1883 settlement, a full-service Breslau library branch, and the 2023-2027 Strategic Plan.

Council approved several construction and procurement items, including a new airport café and a 6-storey residential development at 82 Wilson Ave. It also decided the Region will opt out of administering blue box service from March 2, 2024. Staff will report back on a delegate's request to waive a planning fee.

decisions.detail: Council approved a heavy truck ban on downtown Cambridge streets to move through trucks onto McQueen Shaver Boulevard {{vote:m11}}, with noise walls, a review of further bans and a truck route policy review.

decisions.item: Basic income and social assistance advocacy
decisions.detail: Council asked the province to raise and index social assistance rates and called on both senior governments to implement a national guaranteed liveable basic income {{vote:m22}}.

decisions.item: Conestoga College U-Pass and Associate Medical Officer of Health
decisions.detail: Council supported in principle a Conestoga U-Pass as early as September 2024, subject to 2024 budget approval, and appointed Dr. Adelle Chang On as Associate Medical Officer of Health {{vote:m17}}.
Council approved a tentative Memorandum of Settlement for office, clerical and technical staff for July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2026 {{vote:m19}}.
The Region will opt out of administering blue box service at its March 2, 2024 transition date, with staff continuing collection for sites not covered by the new regulation {{vote:m16}}.
Council approved converting the Breslau Satellite Branch to a full-service library in the lower level of the Breslau Community Centre {{vote:m12}}.

decisions.item: Strategic Plan and Administration and Finance recommendations
decisions.detail: Council approved the 2023-2027 Strategic Plan, an updated Emergency Management By-Law, and continued electronic participation for councillors {{vote:m13}}.
Council accepted a tender for the 6-storey residential development at 82 Wilson Ave, Kitchener, and approved debenture authority of $23,615,000.

debate: On the truck ban, staff said banning trucks on Concession Street falls outside the Region's truck route policy because the alternate route is too long. They said it would raise truck numbers on McQueen Shaver enough to warrant a full noise wall, and recommended a policy review. Staff also expected some pushback from the trucking industry.

Staff said a short section of Ainslie Street stays open to trucks. Banning it would push trucks onto long detours or onto township roads and a footbridge with weight limits. One councillor asked about speed on McQueen Shaver. Staff said there are no design changes planned, because the road should attract trucks away from residential streets. Councillors stressed enforcement and monitoring.

Delegates for Basic Income Waterloo Region said basic income is needed, doable and affordable. They cited rising food bank use, social assistance rates below the poverty line, and health improvements in the Ontario pilot. One delegate said the federal net cost could be covered by tax changes. Councillors who spoke supported the motion, citing inequality and the cancelled pilot.

A planning consultant asked Council to waive a $7,000 Official Plan Amendment review fee for a Cambridge property owner. The delegate noted that Cambridge had waived its own fee and that the Region's conditions were already met. Staff said Regional by-laws do not allow such waivers, and Council asked for a staff report.

A Conestoga Students Inc. delegate supported the U-Pass, citing student survey support and savings for students. Staff said service changes, including better service to the skilled trades campus, would come through the 2024 budget. One councillor noted the strategic plan did not name fiscal responsibility explicitly, and staff said it sits under the fourth pillar.
